action_description: Monitor pest populations and implement pest control measures as necessary. Biological control using Trichogramma spp. and Metarhizium spp. is recommended.
Monitor psyllid populations. Use biological control measures where possible. Monitor soil moisture and implement irrigation where necessary. Miticide applications may be required.
Monitor psyllid populations. Use biological control measures where possible. Area-wide spraying may help slow the spread of Huanglongbing (HLB) in newly planted fields.
Increase monitoring and implement preventive pest management measures. Maintain drainage systems and continue regular monitoring and control activities.
Monitor fields two to three times per week. Preventive treatments are recommended where appropriate.
Monitor fields two to three times per week. Apply preventive or control measures during the early stages of infestation.
Monitor pests at least twice per week and implement an Integrated Pest Management (IPM) programme. Monitor soil moisture and practice water conservation techniques such as mulching.
Monitor for diseases and implement an Integrated Pest Management (IPM) programme. Ensure proper land preparation and drainage. Plant on raised beds or ridges where appropriate.
Maintain adequate irrigation and apply mulch to conserve soil moisture. Paint tree trunks with white paint or lime wash to reduce sunscald.

Coconut: Monitor for coconut weevils, mites, and red spider mites. Use traps where appropriate. Apply Neem X, Bioneem (5 mL/L of water), sulphur (5–10 mL/L of water), or agricultural oil (1.5 L plus 1 L detergent per 100 L of water) as recommended. Remove and destroy trees infected with Phytophthora or Red Ring Disease, and control coconut weevils to reduce nematode transmission.
Avocado: Apply sulphocalcic broth or Bordeaux mixture for the prevention and control of pests and diseases. Mix 2 litres of the prepared broth with 18 litres of water before application.
Soursop: Remove and properly dispose of damaged fruits. Bag fruits where practical and apply sulphocalcic broth for insect and disease management.
Cacao: Reduce excessive shade by maintaining appropriate tree height. Remove diseased pods promptly and dispose of them properly.
Pineapple: Monitor fields regularly for pests and diseases, and implement appropriate control measures when necessary.

Ensure proper drainage in low-lying or waterlogged areas. Maintain an effective pest and disease management programme using approved organic or synthetic pesticides where appropriate. Consult the Ministry of Agriculture, local agro-dealers, or the Belize Agricultural Health Authority (BAHA) for recommendations on suitable pesticides, application rates, and assistance with pest and disease identification.
